# MeshPart

- Inherits [`BasePart`](basepart.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("MeshPart")`

A part whose shape is a mesh imported from a model file. One `MeshPart` is one mesh; a model made of several pieces is several `MeshPart`s.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CollisionFidelity` | `Enum.CollisionFidelity` | — | read/write | How closely the collision shape follows the mesh. `Box` collides as the mesh's bounding box. Every other value collides as the mesh's convex hull.<br><br>Until the mesh has loaded, the part collides as its bounding box. A mesh too thin or too small to form a solid also collides as its bounding box. The property reads back the value you set. |
| `MeshContent` | `Content` | — | read/write | The model file this part draws, as an `asset://` path to a glTF file. Setting it replaces the mesh. If the file fails to load, the part keeps its previous mesh and the error is logged.<br><br>Set from a script, it also sets `MeshSize` to the size of the mesh, and `Size` too if it is still (1, 1, 1), so the part draws and collides at the mesh's own size. See `MeshSize`. |
| `MeshSize` | `vector` | `vector.create(1, 1, 1)` | read/write | The size of the mesh as it was authored, in meters. The part is scaled by `Size` divided by `MeshSize`, so setting `Size` to twice `MeshSize` draws and collides the mesh at twice its authored size.<br><br>Setting `MeshContent` from a script sets this to the size of the new mesh at once, read from the game's imported content, and sets `Size` to the same value if `Size` is still (1, 1, 1). On a client, this happens only for parts the client made; a part the server made takes both values from the server. The editor sets it when you import or drop a mesh, and it is saved with the scene. You can set it yourself to stretch the mesh. Each component must be greater than 0. |
| `PoseFrom` | `MeshPart?` | `nil` | read/write | Another skinned `MeshPart` whose pose this one copies. Set it on a piece of armor, hair, a glove or a held item so that the piece moves with the body it is worn on.<br><br>Every joint that both meshes have follows the leader's joint exactly, whatever moved it: a clip, an animation graph, an `IKControl`, a `SpringBone` or a ragdoll. Joints are matched by name. A joint that only this mesh has stays at rest relative to its parent, unless an animation playing on the leader has a track for it.<br><br>A mesh that follows a leader has no physics body of its own: it does not collide, and raycasts pass through it. It keeps its own `SpringBone` chains and morph targets. It follows nothing if it names itself, if the leaders form a loop, or if the leader has no skeleton. To attach an item that shares no joints with the body, parent it under a `Bone` of the body instead. |

## Methods

### `ClearMorphWeight(name: string)`

Removes the weight that `SetMorphWeight` set for one morph target. From the next frame, the target follows the playing clips again, or the weight the file gives at rest.

### `GetMorphTargets(): { string }`

Returns the names of this mesh's morph targets (shape keys), in the order the file lists them. Returns an empty array if the mesh has none, or if its file has not loaded yet. To be sure the mesh is loaded, call `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync` first.

### `GetMorphWeight(name: string): number`

Returns the weight this part is drawn with for one morph target, on this machine. That is the value a script set, or else the value from the clips playing on the mesh, or else the weight the file gives at rest. Returns 0 for a name the mesh does not have.

### `SetMorphWeight(name: string, weight: number)`

Sets the weight of one morph target of this mesh. 0 is the mesh at rest and 1 is the full shape. Values outside that range are allowed, and several targets add together.

The weight applies only on the machine where the script runs. It is not replicated and not recorded in a replay, so set it in a client script. It overrides what a playing clip sets for the same target until you call `ClearMorphWeight`.

Raises an error for a name the mesh does not have, once the mesh has loaded. A weight set before the mesh loads is kept and applied when it arrives.
